inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped strength-of-schedule report computes geometric means with EXP(AVG(LOG(metric))) and reverses the defensive metric with a negated aggregate before casting the rounded values to numeric.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored division-strength report with new table and column names, fixed positive metrics, and MariaDB DECIMAL casts. The source's PostgreSQL ::numeric syntax is translated to CAST(... AS DECIMAL(10,3)).

fixture_notes: Division 10 has strength values 2 and 8, offense values 4 and 16, and defense values 2 and 8; division 20 has one row. All logarithm inputs are strictly positive, and each group has a stable integer key.
determinism_notes: All IDs and metric values are fixed, each division/year pair is unique, and the final grouped read orders by division ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE division_strength (sample_id INT PRIMARY KEY, division_id INT NOT NULL, season_year INT NOT NULL, strength_metric DECIMAL(10,3) NOT NULL, offense_metric DECIMAL(10,3) NOT NULL, defense_metric DECIMAL(10,3) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT division_id, season_year, CAST(ROUND(EXP(AVG(LOG(strength_metric))), 3) AS DECIMAL(10,3)) AS geometric_strength, CAST(ROUND(EXP(AVG(LOG(offense_metric))), 3) AS DECIMAL(10,3)) AS geometric_offense, CAST(ROUND(EXP(-AVG(LOG(defense_metric))), 3) AS DECIMAL(10,3)) AS inverse_geometric_defense FROM division_strength GROUP BY division_id, season_year ORDER BY division_id
